encounters.cc: Follow-up visit after completing routine bone health evaluation with reports of height loss of 3 cm over several years and occasional mild back pain with prolonged standing or walking.

lines: Follow-up visit after completing routine bone health evaluation with reports of height loss of 3 cm over several years and occasional mild back pain with prolonged standing or walking.
She is otherwise in good health but notes that she has shrunk about 3 cm in height over the past few years.
She also reports occasional mild back pain that comes and goes, especially after standing or walking for long periods.
She has no history of falls or fractures.
She went through menopause at age 51 and did not use hormone replacement therapy.
Her only medication is a daily multivitamin.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
She has a history of smoking but quit 15 years ago.
She consumes one glass of wine per week and does not exercise regularly.
She eats a balanced diet but does not take any calcium or vitamin D supplements.
Her physical exam reveals kyphosis and mild tenderness to percussion over the lower thoracic spine.
Laboratory studies are within normal limits.
Bone densitometry reveals decreased mineral density at both the lumbar spine and femoral neck.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset odynophagia and retrosternal chest pain exacerbated by swallowing solids over the past 2 days.

lines: Sudden-onset odynophagia and retrosternal chest pain exacerbated by swallowing solids over the past 2 days.
This 72-year-old female with osteoporosis presents to the emergency department one month following her initial bone health evaluation.
She reports that the pain is exacerbated when she swallows, especially with solid foods.
She denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in her diet.
Her medical history is significant for osteoporosis, for which she takes alendronate once weekly, and chronic knee osteoarthritis managed with ibuprofen as needed.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
She does not smoke or consume alcohol.
On physical examination, she is afebrile, and her vital signs are within normal limits.
Her oropharyngeal examination is unremarkable, and there is no cervical lymphadenopathy.
Laboratory tests reveal normal complete blood count and basic metabolic panel.
An upper endoscopy is performed, which shows a localized, well-demarcated ulcerative lesion in the mid-esophagus without evidence of bleeding.

encounters.cc: Acute lower back pain for 2 days after lifting a heavy pot of water, described as sharp and constant without radiation.

lines: Acute lower back pain for 2 days after lifting a heavy pot of water, described as sharp and constant without radiation.

The patient is a 73-year-old female with a known history of osteoporosis and prior reports of height loss and mechanical back pain who presents with a 2-day history of acute lower back pain after lifting a heavy pot of water.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant, with no radiation.
She denies any recent trauma, fever, bowel or bladder incontinence, or weight loss.
She has a history of osteoporosis.
She takes calcium and vitamin D supplements.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
Alcohol: Minimal (one glass of wine weekly).
On physical examination, she has localized tenderness over the T12 vertebra but no ecchymosis or swelling.
Neurological examination, including motor strength, reflexes, and sensation, is normal.
A lateral spine X-ray shows a wedge-shaped deformity of the T12 vertebral body.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe lower back pain while lifting a heavy box earlier today, localized to midline lower back without radiation.

lines: Sudden onset of severe lower back pain while lifting a heavy box earlier today, localized to midline lower back without radiation.

The patient is a 74-year-old female with osteoporosis and prior T12 compression fracture who presents with sudden onset of severe lower back pain that began while she was lifting a heavy box earlier in the day.
She describes the pain as sharp and localized to the midline of her lower back, with no radiation.
She denies any recent trauma, fever, bowel or bladder incontinence, or weight loss.
- Acute osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture of T12 (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
Her medical history is significant for osteoporosis.
She takes calcium and vitamin D supplements.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
Alcohol: Minimal (one glass of wine weekly).
Her vital signs are within normal limits
On physical examination, she has tenderness to palpation over the T12 vertebral body.
There is no neurological deficit, and straight leg raise test is negative.
An X-ray of the thoracic and lumbar spine reveals a compression fracture of the T12 vertebral body.

encounters.cc: Severe left hip pain following a mechanical fall at home after tripping over a rug.

lines: Severe left hip pain following a mechanical fall at home after tripping over a rug.
The patient, with established osteoporosis and prior T12 compression fractures in 2021 and 2022, presents with severe left hip pain.
She reports that she tripped over a rug and landed directly on her left side.
- Acute osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture of T12 (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
She has a history of osteoporosis.
She takes calcium and vitamin D supplements.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
Alcohol: Minimal (one glass of wine weekly).
On examination, her left leg appears shortened and is externally rotated.
She is unable to bear weight on the left leg.
An x-ray of the left hip shows a displaced fracture of the femoral neck with disruption of the normal cortical contour and irregular lucency at the fracture plane.

lines: Watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and low-grade fever for 3 days following recent hospitalization.

encounters.cc: Watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and low-grade fever with 6-8 unformed bowel movements daily for 3 days.

lines: Watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and low-grade fever with 6-8 unformed bowel movements daily for 3 days.
This 76-year-old female with osteoporosis, COPD, and prior C. difficile infection presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and low-grade fever.
She reports having 6-8 unformed bowel movements per day.

Abdominal examination reveals mild diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Her white blood cell count is 15,000/µL, and a stool sample is positive for C. difficile toxin and glutamate dehydrogenase antigen.

encounters.cc: Sudden episode of vaginal bleeding in a postmenopausal woman with no recent trauma.

lines: Sudden episode of vaginal bleeding in a postmenopausal woman with no recent trauma.
This patient with prior fragility fractures presents with sudden episode of vaginal bleeding that she found quite distressing.
There has been no recent trauma.
- Acute osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture of T12 (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- Displaced fracture of left femoral neck (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Severe Clostridioides difficile infection without toxic megacolon (diagnosed 2023-09-15)
Until then they were monthly and regular.
She has 3 children born via spontaneous vaginal delivery.
She has had mammograms every 2 years which have all been normal.
- Mother: Hip fracture due to osteoporosis
She is sexually active exclusively with her husband of 55 years.
An ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and a 1.3-cm heterogenous mass in the right ovary.
